preconditions.description: The input integer n is between 1 and 100,000 inclusive.

postconditions.expression: stdout.startswith('YES') == (any(all(i in range(n) for i in prefix_product) and len(set(prefix_product)) == n for prefix_product in (list(accumulate(permutation, lambda x, y: x * y % n)) for permutation in permutations(range(1, n + 1))))
postconditions.description: The output starts with 'YES' if there exists a permutation of [1, 2, ..., n] such that its prefix product sequence is a permutation of [0, 1, ..., n - 1], otherwise it starts with 'NO'.

postconditions.expression: stdout.startswith('NO') == (not any(all(i in range(n) for i in prefix_product) and len(set(prefix_product)) == n for prefix_product in (list(accumulate(permutation, lambda x, y: x * y % n)) for permutation in permutations(range(1, n + 1)))))
postconditions.description: The output starts with 'NO' if there does not exist a permutation of [1, 2, ..., n] such that its prefix product sequence is a permutation of [0, 1, ..., n - 1].

postconditions.expression: stdout.startswith('YES') and len(stdout.splitlines()) == n + 1 and all(int(line) in range(1, n + 1) for line in stdout.splitlines()[1:]) and len(set(int(line) for line in stdout.splitlines()[1:])) == n
postconditions.description: If the output starts with 'YES', it is followed by n lines, each containing a unique integer between 1 and n inclusive.
